title: Publish the daemon command surface on the @moe/daemon root
description:
Objective: publish the committed daemon command surface on the @moe/daemon package root so the Foundation canary and any external consumer can drive it. Created by architect-0b81de40 2026-08-09. This is the THIRD instance of one recurring defect, and the two prior fixes are the template: task-8ee125d0 did it for @moe/scheduler (commit 239aa4f) and task-53680e91 for @moe/runner.

WHY THIS EXISTS. apps/daemon/package.json pins "exports": {".": "./src/index.ts"} - an EXCLUSIVE map, so no deep subpath import reaches around it at runtime or under moduleResolution NodeNext. But apps/daemon/src/index.ts exports exactly ONE function, evaluateGraphPreviewRequestBytes, explicitly advisoryOnly:true / authority:"NONE". Meanwhile six directories of real, committed, tested command surface sit unreachable beneath it: bootstrap/, goals/, planning/, work/, http/, recovery/.

MEASURED ON DISK 2026-08-09: apps/daemon/src/index.ts has 6 export statements, all graph-preview. Unreachable from the root: BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA_VERSION, BOOTSTRAP_REQUEST_KEYS, BOOTSTRAP_REFUSAL_CODES, decodeBootstrapRequestBytes (bootstrap-contracts.ts); GOAL_HANDLERS (goal-services.ts:66); PLANNING_HANDLERS (planning-services.ts:156); claimWork, parseWorkRequest, WORK_SCHEMA_VERSION (work/); EVENT_STREAM_REFUSAL_CODES, MAX_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE (http/); DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS, DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES, evaluateDoctorCommandBytes (recovery/).

THIS IS THE CANARY'S BLOCKER. worker-e46fb0dc blocked task-97554aa4 at step 5 with exactly this diagnosis: "no daemon command surface to drive ... the three handler tables are unreachable from the package root, the same exports-map wall that blocked task-ba3a45f9". Against J1's three human actions (design line 1095), goal.create exists but is unreachable. Publishing this surface is what lets the canary's journey half proceed.

Deliverable: a curated named-export block in apps/daemon/src/index.ts in the style that file and packages/runner/src/index.ts already use - named exports grouped per module, types in the same block via the `type` modifier, every specifier written with the .js extension per NodeNext - covering the command kinds, request decoders, handler tables, refusal-code vocabularies and result types a consumer needs to drive bootstrap, goal, planning, work, event-stream and doctor commands and to discriminate every branch of their result unions. Read the modules before naming a single symbol; do not guess.

NOT in scope: changing ANY behaviour in any daemon module; exporting test-only modules (http/event-stream-fixtures.ts is fixtures - do NOT export it); adding a .js bridge (apps/daemon has none and needs none, unlike @moe/store); touching packages/**; any package.json or lockfile edit.

Hard dependencies: none. Every surface named above is committed at HEAD.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/index.ts and apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts (new).
Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/src/index.ts exports the daemon command surface such that a consumer can, without any deep subpath import, decode a bootstrap request, reach the goal and planning handler tables, parse and claim work, read the event-stream refusal vocabulary, and evaluate a doctor command — naming every parameter type and every union branch of every exported function's return type.

A new apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts imports the package ROOT specifier @moe/daemon (never a relative or deep path) and asserts per symbol that the export is present and of the expected typeof, so a dropped export fails by name rather than by a vague count.

The same test asserts set equality between Object.keys of the namespace and a hand-written expected export-name list, so both a removed export AND an unreviewed addition go red. The list is hand-transcribed from the modules, never derived from the namespace under test.

The advisory envelope discipline survives publication: a test asserts through the published surface that results carrying no authority still report advisoryOnly:true and authority:"NONE", so publishing cannot silently promote an advisory result into an authoritative one.
No test-only module is exported — http/event-stream-fixtures.ts in particular stays internal — asserted by the set-equality list.

Zero behaviour change: git diff shows apps/daemon/src/index.ts as the only modified non-test file, no .js bridge is added, and the pre-existing daemon suite passes with a test count greater than or equal to the pre-task count, stated as an explicit before/after number.
pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck all exit 0; committed paths are exactly the two owned files.
taskRails: Re-export only. This task changes what is REACHABLE, never what any function DOES. No .ts file other than index.ts may be edited. If a symbol seems to need a signature change to be exportable, report_blocked rather than editing a daemon service module.

Read the modules before naming a symbol; do not guess export names and do not copy them from this description without verifying each one on disk (skill: explore-before-assume). Six directories landed from six different tasks within hours of each other and are still settling.
Never export a test-only module. http/event-stream-fixtures.ts stays internal; exporting fixtures puts test code on the runtime surface.
Prefer curated named exports over a blanket `export *`, so the published seam stays a reviewed decision rather than whatever the modules happen to export next week.
Add no .js bridge. apps/daemon has none and needs none — that convention belongs to @moe/store alone, and a partial sweep would be invisible to the vitest gate.
Assert against the production surface obtained through the @moe/daemon root import, never against a locally re-declared type or a fixture copy.

Keep the entry point focused: target <=250 lines, split before 400. If the added exports push index.ts past 250 lines, extract a per-area re-export module that index.ts re-exports rather than letting the entry point sprawl.
Commit by explicit pathspec only — git commit -- apps/daemon/src/index.ts apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts. Several agents share this working directory; verify with git show --stat afterwards.

implementationPlan.description: Record the pre-task daemon suite file/test/pass/fail/skip count, then create the RED package-root surface contract in apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts. Import `* as daemon` and every tested type only from `@moe/daemon`, never a relative/deep daemon path. Hand-transcribe an alphabetized 31-value `[name, typeof]` table and assert both exact set equality with Object.keys and one named typeof case per value; guard the table with exact cardinality 31 so it cannot silently empty. The approved runtime values are the existing evaluateGraphPreviewRequestBytes plus BOOTSTRAP_COMMAND_KINDS, BOOTSTRAP_HANDLERS, BOOTSTRAP_REFUSAL_CODES, BOOTSTRAP_REQUEST_KEYS, BOOTSTRAP_SCHEMA_VERSION, SERVICE_REFUSED_BY, PREREQUISITE_REFUSAL_CODES, decodeBootstrapRequestBytes, runBootstrapCommand, GOAL_HANDLERS, PLANNING_HANDLERS, WORK_SCHEMA_VERSION, WORK_COMMANDS, CLAIM_LEGS, SLOT_CEILING_LEG, WORK_LEGS, WORK_LAYERS, WORK_ERROR_CODES, WORK_AUTHORITY_LABELS, parseWorkRequest, claimWork, MAX_EVENT_PAGE_SIZE, EVENT_STREAM_REFUSAL_CODES, EVENT_STREAM_LAYER, readEventPage, resumeFromSnapshot, DOCTOR_RECOVERY_SCHEMA_VERSION, DOCTOR_COMMAND_KINDS, DOCTOR_ERROR_CODES, and evaluateDoctorCommandBytes. Add an explicit non-empty forbidden-fixture list (PROJECTION, SUBSCRIBER, SNAPSHOT_CHECKPOINT, STATE_DIGEST, LEDGER_EVENT_IDS, ledgerIdsUpTo, streamPort) and assert none is an own property of the root namespace. Run only this new test and confirm RED names the missing approved exports.

Add compile-time root-surface coverage to the same test and implement the curated re-exports in apps/daemon/src/index.ts. Use grouped named blocks with `.js` specifiers and `type` modifiers from each verified module; never export-star. Export the full type closure needed to name every parameter and union arm: from bootstrap contracts—BootstrapCommandKind, BootstrapRefusalCode, BootstrapRefusedBy, BootstrapRequest, BootstrapInputRejected, BootstrapRequestRefused, BootstrapRequestAccepted, BootstrapDecodeRefusal, BootstrapDecodeResult; from bootstrap ledger—ServiceRefusedBy, PrerequisiteRefusalCode, DurableAggregate, DurableLedger, ServiceAccepted, ServiceRefused, ServiceOutcome, HandlerContext, CommandHandler, HandlerTable; from work kernel—WorkCommand, ClaimLeg, WorkLeg, WorkLayer, WorkErrorCode, WorkAuthorityLabel, WorkFailure, ClaimSuccessors, WorkInputRejected, WorkRefused, WorkGranted, WorkApplied, WorkContextView, WorkResult; from work ingress—WorkRequestEnvelope and WorkRequestParse; from event-stream contract—StreamCursor, StreamSnapshot, StreamEvent, StreamPage, StreamGap, StreamRefused, StreamSeated, StreamReadResult, StreamSeatResult, StreamPageRequest, StreamReseatRequest, SubscriptionPort, EventStreamRefusalCode, WireCursor, WireEvent, WireSnapshot, EventPageFrame, EventGapFrame, EventRefusedFrame, EventReseatedFrame, EventReadFrame, EventResumeFrame, EventReadRequest, EventResumeRequest; from doctor—DoctorCommandKind, DoctorErrorCode, DoctorInputRejected, DoctorRequestInvalid, DoctorAuthorityStale, DoctorReported, DoctorProposed, DoctorCommandResult. Use expectTypeOf/type equalities against the root functions/tables to exercise every parameter, return union, and branch type without local redeclarations. Through the root call evaluateGraphPreviewRequestBytes on `{}` bytes and assert the exact REQUEST_INVALID / GRAPH_PREVIEW_REQUEST_INVALID refusal plus advisoryOnly:true and authority:"NONE". Make the focused test green, keep index.ts <=250 physical lines, and edit no other production module, package file, or bridge.

Perform the single adversarial review over the two owned files. Verify every exported name against its defining module and every type against the actual signature; ensure general HTTP adapter helpers, bootstrap ledger mutation helpers, work internals, and all `*.test.ts`/fixture modules remain absent. Check that type-only exports add zero runtime keys, all handler tables are defined objects, all approved functions are callable values, and the graph preview advisory test reads the production root rather than a helper. Snapshot index.ts outside the repository and record its git hash; temporarily remove GOAL_HANDLERS to prove the named typeof and set-equality loss axes go red, restore exact bytes, then temporarily add an unapproved safe production export such as HTTP_BOUNDARY_ERROR_CODES to prove the addition axis goes red, restore again. Finally mutate REQUEST_INVALID_RESULT's advisoryOnly or authority field and prove the published advisory-discipline case goes red. Restore in finally paths, verify each original hash, confirm index.ts remains <=250 lines, and leave no scratch/generated files.

Run the one final foreground verification command exactly: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck`. Record exit 0 and explicit before/after daemon file/test/pass/fail/skip counts, showing the final count is at least the baseline and accounting exactly for every new index-surface case. Inspect `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/index.ts apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts` to prove re-export-only scope, run `git status --porcelain`, unstage foreign entries without altering them, and stage/commit only the two owned paths with `git commit -- apps/daemon/src/index.ts apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts`. Verify `git show --stat` contains exactly those two paths and no package/bridge/service module before calling moe.complete_task.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Publish one explicit reviewed root seam, following the landed @moe/scheduler and @moe/runner fixes. Deep exports, package.json changes, blanket export-star, behavior edits, and test-fixture exports are rejected. The curated surface includes only the public command-driving seams and their complete type closure: bootstrap decode/run/handlers, goal/planning handler tables, work parse/claim vocabularies, event-stream read/resume contracts, doctor evaluation, and the existing graph-preview advisory operation. General HTTP adapter internals and bootstrap ledger helper functions are not required to drive the named seams and remain internal.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Current apps/daemon/src/index.ts is 97 physical lines and has exactly one runtime export, evaluateGraphPreviewRequestBytes, plus its graph-preview result types. Verified defining modules and signatures: decodeBootstrapRequestBytes -> BootstrapDecodeResult; runBootstrapCommand(SqliteEventStore, unknown, HandlerTable?) -> ServiceOutcome; GOAL_HANDLERS and PLANNING_HANDLERS are HandlerTable; parseWorkRequest -> WorkRequestParse; claimWork -> WorkResult; readEventPage(SubscriptionPort, EventReadRequest) -> EventReadFrame; resumeFromSnapshot(SubscriptionPort, EventResumeRequest) -> EventResumeFrame; evaluateDoctorCommandBytes -> DoctorCommandResult. apps/daemon's Vitest script deliberately uses `--root . --config package.json src`, because the repository root config does not discover apps/**. This task adds no .js bridge and relies on the existing daemon build/test convention.
planningNotes.risks: Keep runtime values and type-only names distinct so Object.keys remains the hand-reviewed 31-value set. Avoid `CommandHandler` collisions by publishing the bootstrap handler type only; the general HTTP adapter stays internal. The type closure must include every discriminated union arm and every function parameter, but need not re-export upstream @moe/contracts/@moe/store types already available from their own roots. Root publication eagerly evaluates the referenced modules under Vitest, so any cycle/undefined value must fail the per-symbol typeof checks. The forbidden fixture runtime names are PROJECTION, SUBSCRIBER, SNAPSHOT_CHECKPOINT, STATE_DIGEST, LEDGER_EVENT_IDS, ledgerIdsUpTo, and streamPort; none may appear.
